attribution.note: Marcus presents this assessment in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the retrospective scope and qualified appearance of increasing reliance.

contract.note: The contract reasonably distinguishes announcements from completed financing, but applies plain-reading scoring to hedged language. The policy permits that approach only for firm claims; 'seemed' does not supply a firm commitment.

evidence.note: This dated company disclosure supports the apparent pattern through proposed investment linked to NVIDIA deployment. It does not establish completed financing or an increasing industry financing share.

The company disclosure identifies another supplier-investment relationship alongside compute purchase commitments within the observation window. It supports apparent prominence, without proving realized funding.

The report qualifies broader dependence claims but does not measure whether circular financing became more prominent. Predominant cash-flow financing can coexist with increasing circular arrangements.
The contemporaneous report establishes that the proposed NVIDIA investment was nonbinding. This limits conclusions about completed financing without negating the announced pattern.

reviews.rationale: Marcus qualified this observation with 'seemed.' The policy excludes hedged claims from scoring and bars using a plain-reading contract to overcome that qualification. The disclosures provide a factual basis for the apparent pattern, but cannot turn his qualified assessment into a firm claim.
